#8/normal.conflict: DISPUTED CELL, shipped adjudicated rather than silently. The two transcription sources print this one cell differently: both print drill #9, one prints d = 0.196 (which is drill #9's own tabulated diameter) and the other 0.190 (which is not any drill size - it is the #10 screw's nominal diameter). The agreeing datum is the drill designation, and in both sources every other row's diameter column is exactly its drill's diameter, so the cell ships as drill #9 / d 0.196 and the rejected value 0.190 is named here. Because its sources disagreed, this cell answers corroborated: false - two sources that do not agree are not corroboration, and reporting it as corroborated said the transcription had been checked when what actually happened is that a disagreement was adjudicated.

notes: ASME B18.2.8 names the three series close / normal / loose; ISO 273 names the same idea fine / medium / coarse. hole_standards accepts both spellings and reports the requested standard's.

THERE IS MORE THAN ONE PUBLISHED INCH CLEARANCE CHART, and they are not roundings of each other. The traditional Machinery's-Handbook 'close fit / free fit' table gives a #10 screw 0.196 / 0.201 in; another widely-reprinted chart gives 0.196 / 0.204 / 0.221. B18.2.8 gives 0.206 / 0.221 / 0.238. Those are three conventions, not three transcriptions, so this file names the standard it transcribes in its header and does not blend them. Both sources above print the B18.2.8 numbers.

d is the printed nominal hole diameter, which is the tabulated drill's own diameter; the standard also gives a max for each cell (e.g. #10 close is 0.206-0.211) which is a tolerance, not a second size, and is not stored. drill is the designation the shop reads - part of the callout, not a rounding of a millimetre value.

One cell the two sources printed differently: #8 NORMAL. Both print drill #9; one prints 0.196 (which is drill #9's tabulated diameter) and the other 0.190 (which is not any drill size, and is the #10 screw's nominal diameter). The agreeing datum is the drill designation, so the cell ships with drill #9 / 0.196 and the disagreement is recorded on the cell rather than resolved silently. It ships DISPUTED, not agreed: hole_standards answers corroborated: false for that cell and carries the adjudication in conflicts, while its two neighbours in the same row answer corroborated: true. Two sources that disagree are not corroboration.

PROVENANCE IS PER CELL AND IS ENFORCED PER CELL. Every cell above - each fit of each size - is named in a provenance group or scope with the sources it was transcribed from. There is no file-wide default AND no row-level fallback: both are the same mistake at different depths, and covering by row let a cell added later inherit that row's citations (measured on the thread table, where an undeclared M12x1.5 pitch answered corroborated: true over two publications). A cell added from one publication cannot inherit these citations - hole_standards refuses to load the file and names the cell. The file-level `sources` list is the union over the cells and is a claim about none of them: source 2 backs only the #4 and #10 spot checks.
